propositions: The judge's Pass-2/Pass-3 decision (block/advisory/dropped/indeterminate) must be self-consistent across repeated runs: Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.6 AND raw agreement ≥ 0.8 over N=50 G6/E4/T3 cohort findings × 3 votes each, else R5 is blocked.
Plan section-order permutations must not flip the gate verdict (PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE): Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.6 AND raw agreement ≥ 0.8 over N=14 plans × 3 distinct permutations, else R3 is blocked.

Infra-INDETERMINATE outcomes (llm_unavailable or verify_failed flags) are execution failures, not stable judge decisions, and must be excluded and re-run; genuine judge-INDETERMINATE (neither flag) counts as a valid agreement category.
Re-judge inputs (plan text + finding records) must be frozen in committed files to enable reproducible self-consistency measurement independent of live ticket stores.

Section-order permutations must be deterministic and reproducible via pinned per-plan seed, with permutation 0 always the identity and exactly 3 distinct orderings generated per qualifying plan (≥3 top-level sections).

Experiment A measures existing judge stochasticity via Pass-2/Pass-3; Experiment B measures gate-verdict stability via the public review_plan entrypoint against a throwaway ticket-store clone, neither modifying production code.
